# Results — Study 742 (Friday-17th / *Venerdì 17*)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **Italy's
FTSE MIB trades weak on Friday the 17th** (*Venerdì 17*, the Italian unlucky day and the
Latin-market cousin of the desk's [Friday-13th](../../163-friday-13th/) teardown). Signal:
the daily close-to-close log-return of the FTSE MIB (local, EUR, price-only) on every
Friday-the-17th since 1998, tested against all other Fridays, with a random-calendar
placebo, a look-elsewhere Bonferroni sweep, and a costed short. Cross-checked on EWI
(US-listed, USD, total-return). Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python
examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete
calendar month). Fingerprint `e5483c326431` (FTSE MIB + EWI, one combined panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Primary tape | `FTSEMIB.MI` (FTSE MIB) — yfinance daily closes, **EUR, price-only** (index, no dividend adjustment), 7,276 returns, 1998-01-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Vehicle tape | `EWI` (iShares MSCI Italy) — yfinance daily closes, **USD, total-return** (dividends reinvested), 7,619 returns, 1996-03-19 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **pure date arithmetic**: Venerdì 17 = weekday == Friday **and** day-of-month == 17. Known before the open → **zero look-ahead**, no estimation lag. |
| Events | **49** Venerdì 17s on the MIB tape, **52** on the (longer) EWI tape — ~1.7 per year |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the return across independent, non-overlapping events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Welch contrast vs all other Fridays; Wilson down-day interval; a 20-seed × 500-draw random-calendar placebo; a Bonferroni sweep over Friday slots 17 ± 7k = {3, 10, 17, 24, 31} |
| Execution / costs | short established at the **prior** close (calendar-known → no look-ahead), covered at the 17th's close; one round trip = 2× one-way cost (5 bps) × NAV **+ 2 bps one-day short borrow** = 12 bps breakeven |

**Currency / adjustment, labelled:** the FTSE MIB series is **price-only, in euro** — the
purest read of Italian sentiment. EWI is **total-return, in US dollars**, so it blends the
Italian tape with the EUR/USD cross; it is the tradable cross-check, not the clean
local-sentiment read. Neither is ever quoted under the other's banner.

## The honest test — Venerdì 17 vs all other Fridays

**Primary result: the unlucky day points the *wrong* way.**

| Tape | n | Venerdì-17 mean (bps) | one-sample *t* | vs other Fridays (contrast, Welch *p*) | down-day rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **FTSE MIB** (EUR, price-only) | 49 | **+26.29** | **+1.27** | +28.94 bps, *p* = 0.170 | 23/49 = **46.9%** [33.7%, 60.6%] |
| EWI (USD, total-return) | 52 | +10.07 | +0.52 | +12.49 bps, *p* = 0.531 | 24/52 = 46.2% [33.3%, 59.5%] |

- The FTSE MIB averages **+26.3 bps** on Venerdì 17 — **positive**, i.e. the opposite of
  the fear — and *t* = +1.27 is comfortably inside the noise band. It even **beats** the
  ordinary Friday (−2.65 bps) by +28.9 bps, and that gap is statistically
  indistinguishable from zero (Welch *p* = 0.17).
- The down-day rate is **below 50%** on both tapes: Venerdì 17 is a red day *less* than
  half the time. There is no excess of losses.
- EWI, the USD total-return vehicle, tells the same story one currency over (+10.1 bps,
  *t* = +0.52).

## Random-calendar placebo (20 seeds × 500 draws = 10,000 matched Friday sets)

Draw random sets of *n* **other** Fridays from the same tape (a matched null that holds
any generic Friday-of-the-week effect fixed) and compare the observed Venerdì-17 mean.
Folklore predicts the observed sits in the **left** tail.

| Tape | observed (bps) | null mean (sd) | left-tail *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **FTSE MIB** | +26.29 | −2.81 (20.60) | **0.927** |
| EWI | +10.07 | −2.46 (22.29) | 0.714 |

The observed mean sits out at the **high** end of the null (*p*-left = 0.93 on the MIB) —
the opposite of what the curse predicts. A randomly-chosen Friday is *more* likely to look
weak than Venerdì 17. This is the single cleanest refutation in the study.

## Look-elsewhere — day-of-month Bonferroni sweep (FTSE MIB)

The 17th was chosen by superstition, not pre-registered. Test all five neighbouring Friday
slots (17 ± 7k) and Bonferroni-correct (k = 5):

| Day of month | n | mean (bps) | contrast vs other Fridays | raw *p* | Bonferroni *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **10th** | 47 | **−62.42** | **−62.80** | **0.0130** | **0.0648** |
| 3rd | 47 | +36.75 | +39.72 | 0.0473 | 0.2364 |
| **17th** | 49 | **+26.29** | **+28.94** | **0.1703** | **0.8515** |
| 24th | 47 | −44.62 | −44.39 | 0.2185 | 1.0000 |
| 31st | 26 | +4.78 | +6.57 | 0.7818 | 1.0000 |

The most extreme middle-Friday is the **10th** (raw *p* = 0.013) — a slot with no
superstition attached — and even it fails to survive Bonferroni (corrected *p* = 0.065).
The **17th has one of the highest raw *p*-values** of the five (0.170). If superstition
predicted anything, it picked the wrong slot — exactly the Friday-the-27th outcome from
study 163.

## Sub-periods (FTSE MIB) — is the null stable?

| Era | n Venerdì-17s | mean (bps) | *t* | contrast vs Fri | Welch *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1998–2012 | 25 | +31.51 | +1.03 | +34.29 | 0.272 |
| 2013–2026 | 24 | +20.84 | +0.74 | +23.34 | 0.419 |
| **Full 1998–2026** | **49** | **+26.29** | **+1.27** | **+28.94** | **0.170** |

Both halves are **positive** — the wrong sign, consistently — and both insignificant.
There is no hidden regime where the curse bites.

## Tradability — the costed short (the folklore bet)

Short into Venerdì 17 (position set at the prior close — calendar-known, no look-ahead),
cover at the 17th's close, pay 2× one-way cost × NAV + one day of short borrow (breakeven
12 bps).

| Tape | n | gross (bps) | *t* | net (bps) | *t* | win rate |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **FTSE MIB** | 49 | **−26.29** | −1.27 | **−38.29** | **−1.85** | 42.9% |
| EWI | 52 | −10.07 | −0.52 | −22.07 | −1.13 | 44.2% |

The short is **negative before costs** (because the day is green on average) and worse
after — a net −38 bps per event on the MIB. There is no edge to charge costs against, and
the naive bet loses outright. Tradability = **Mirage**.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic FTSE-MIB-like tape (business-day index, ~28 years) with a TUNABLE planted
Venerdì-17 effect; no network.

| world | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (effect = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.18** (sd 0.89), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted fear −0.5σ (seed 742) | **−4.51** |
| planted fear −1.0σ (seed 742) | **−8.14** |
| planted fear −2.0σ (seed 742) | **−15.40** |

The detector is silent on the null (0/20 seeds fire) and recovers a planted fear of even
half a daily sigma at *t* = −4.5. The machinery *would* catch a real Venerdì-17 dip; the
real tape simply has none. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support
of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Venerdì 17 on the FTSE MIB is **+26.3 bps** (one-sample *t* = +1.27) —
  *positive*, so the fear has the sign backwards; the down-day rate is 46.9% (below a coin
  flip); the Welch contrast vs other Fridays is insignificant (*p* = 0.17); the
  random-calendar placebo puts the observed mean at the *high* end of the null (left-tail
  *p* = 0.93). EWI concurs (+10.1 bps, *t* = +0.52). Completely indistinguishable from noise,
  and if anything faintly green.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The one bettable expression of the superstition — short the
  unlucky day — loses money gross and net on both tapes (MIB net −38 bps/event, *t* = −1.85;
  EWI net −22 bps). No directional edge exists, so the question of costing one barely arises.
- **Unlucky day? — BUSTED.** On Italy's own market, Venerdì 17 is a slightly *above-average*
  Friday. The most extreme neighbouring slot is the superstition-free 10th, which itself
  dies under Bonferroni; both sample halves agree. The Italian 17th behaves exactly like the
  Anglo 13th (study 163): a deeply-held, universal human dread that leaves no mark on prices.
